player_character_data.backstory: Ambitious son of Marcus Crassus. His 'Aura of Roman Discipline' makes his soldiers unbreakable and his own defenses impenetrable. He seeks to surpass his father's shadow through the systematic destruction of the slave rebellion.
player_character_data.name: Tiberius
features: Aura of Roman Discipline (Lvl 6): Passive +CHA to AC and Saves.
Dueling Fighting Style: +2 dmg with Gladius.
Sentinel Feat: Lock down enemies in combat.
Oath of Conquest (Rome's Oath): Conquering Presence/Guided Strike.
active_effects: Commanding Shouts (Inspirational Focus/Bless, Defensive Formation/Shield of Faith, Lictor's Decree/Command): 3 uses per short rest (0/3 remaining).
Ancestral Fury (Divine Smite (2d8)): Cold, calculated lethality (Force/Psychic damage).
Field Medicine (Lay on Hands): 15 HP pool for legion-based medical training.
Stealth-Friendly Armor: No disadvantage on Stealth checks from Scale Mail.

history: Insulted by Tiberius's suggestion to dicker with pirates

player.notes: Unlike the TV show, Tiberius and Caesar view each other as effective instruments of Crassus's will.
history: Tactical alignment on the Sinuessa blockade
Drank fine wine and discussed Crassus wealth

active_constraints: Caesar is inside Sinuessa (TV Show alignment)

active_missions.title: Shadows of the Port
active_missions.objective: Secure Heracleo's betrayal and silence regarding the sea cave armory.

god_mode_directives.rule: Always display the original D&D 5e spell/ability name in parentheses alongside the Roman reskin (e.g., 'Lictor's Decree (Command)')
Ensure all 'Commanding Shouts' are resolved as mundane leadership/discipline rather than divine magic in narrative descriptions.
Portray Tiberius's sadism through psychological manipulation and the intellectual satisfaction of total control, avoiding overt or cartoonish villainy.
Marcus Crassus must always be portrayed as a stoic, patient strategist who values merit and discipline over ego.
Interpret failed social rolls with Crassus as tactical disagreements or tests of loyalty rather than emotional outbursts.
Always portray the relationship between Tiberius and Julius Caesar as one of mutual respect and strategic partnership.
Interpret Caesar's reactions to Tiberius's plans as professional peer-review rather than antagonistic rivalry.
Portray Marcus Crassus with nuanced paternal warmth; he loves Tiberius as his 'greatest treasure' and shows genuine pride when Tiberius succeeds through discipline and intelligence.

planning_block.context: Ambushed and wounded in Sinuessa alleys; phalanx failed; retreating toward Southern Gate.
planning_block.thinking: The phalanx retreat has failed to provide absolute protection; the smoke and terrain have broken our discipline. I am now double-wounded and my scouts are being picked apart from the balconies. A direct retreat is proving too costly. I must decide whether to use the remaining strength of my elite wedge to clear a balcony and gain the high ground, or risk a full sprint toward the Vanguard lines, abandoning the 'turtle' for speed.

break_and_sprint.description: Order the scouts to break formation and sprint for the Southern Gate, utilizing the smoke for cover rather than shields.
cons: Scouts may be separated and slaughtered
pros: Harder to hit moving targets in smoke

authority_roar_recovery.description: Despite your wounds, project a terrifying aura of Roman inevitability (+8 bonus) to cow the rebels into a momentary hesitation, allowing the wedge to reform.
cons: Fails if rebels are driven by pure zealotry
Requires you to remain stationary for a moment
